name: KY-038 microphone sound sensor
identification: Long narrow black PCB with a blue box-shaped trim potentiometer with a brass screw, an 8-pin chip and 4 angled header pins, and a small round silver microphone capsule at the far end. The KY-037 looks the same with a much larger capsule; say so in the evidence if you cannot tell them apart.

confirmations.question: Read the 4 pin labels printed on the microphone sound sensor. Are they AO, G, + and DO?
confirmations.reason: Clone modules differ. The wiring plan is only valid for a module with exactly these labels.

facts.statement: The module has four pins: analog signal (AO), ground (G), supply (+) and digital signal (DO). Go by the printed labels.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-038, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi, Pico or micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.

A comparator drives DO high when the sound level exceeds the threshold set with the trim potentiometer, and a second LED on the module lights. AO carries the direct measurement, inverted: a higher measured value gives a lower voltage. Powered from 3.3 V, neither output can rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-038, 'Functionality of the sensor'
